findings.title: labels are stale: manifest/taxonomy on disk has changed since labelling
findings.detail: The labelled data records the manifest and taxonomy hashes it was built from, and they no longer match the files on disk. Re-run labelling before trusting anything derived from this zone.

findings.title: ddos/DDoS-LOIC-UDP misses 2 of 3 behavioural expectation(s), worst by 85.3%
findings.detail: The flows carrying this label do not behave the way the label names. Either the window is over the wrong traffic, or the band in expectations.yaml is wrong -- the measured rate and the floor it missed are both reported so the reader can tell which.

evidence.why: Every 2019 reflection vector rides UDP by construction. TCP here means the window caught something other than the reflected flood.
A packet blast, not a session.
A flood converges on a target. 2019 puts 71.8M flows on two victim addresses.

findings.repro:
SELECT count(*) AS flows,
       sum(CASE WHEN (coalesce(proto, '') = 'udp') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS udp_transport,
       approx_count_distinct("id.orig_h") AS distinct_orig_h,
       approx_count_distinct("id.resp_h") AS distinct_resp_h,
       approx_count_distinct("id.orig_p") AS distinct_orig_p,
       approx_count_distinct("id.resp_p") AS distinct_resp_p
FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2018/**/*.parquet', union_by_name=true)
WHERE label_class = 'ddos' AND label_raw = 'DDoS-LOIC-UDP'

findings.title: FTP-BruteForce: 100.0% of flows never sent a byte (192,294 of 192,294)
findings.detail: FTP-BruteForce cannot execute without the attacker sending payload, so these flows are connection attempts labelled as the attack itself. They inflate brute_force and, because they are trivially separable from real attack traffic, they inflate any accuracy figure measured on it.
findings.repro:
SELECT label_executed, count(*) AS flows
FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2018/**/*.parquet', union_by_name=true)
WHERE label_raw = 'FTP-BruteForce'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

findings.title: DoS-SlowHTTPTest: modal destination port is 21 (100.0% of flows), not 80/443/8080
findings.detail: The window labelled DoS-SlowHTTPTest sits on a service its class cannot plausibly be attacking. Either the schedule's endpoints or times are wrong for this attack, or the attack is misnamed in the manifest -- in both cases the flows under this label are not the attack the label describes.
findings.repro:
SELECT "id.resp_p", count(*) AS flows
FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2018/**/*.parquet', union_by_name=true)
WHERE label_raw = 'DoS-SlowHTTPTest'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10

findings.title: 1,753,011 flow(s) report more payload bytes than wire bytes across 2 class(es); benign, botnet materially affected
findings.detail: Payload bytes are a subset of the bytes that crossed the wire, so a flow where orig_bytes exceeds orig_ip_bytes (or resp_bytes exceeds resp_ip_bytes) is arithmetically impossible: Zeek derives the first from TCP sequence numbers, which wrap on scan and RST traffic, and counts the second off the wire, which cannot. These are the same columns that carry the largest label correlation in 2017 (point-biserial -0.442) and the largest attack-class mutual information (0.835), so the corruption sits exactly where the label signal is and every expectation or model built on it inherits the wrap. Use orig_ip_bytes and resp_ip_bytes instead.
findings.repro:
SELECT label_class, count(*) AS n, sum(CASE WHEN "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes" OR "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), sum(CASE WHEN "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), max("orig_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes"), max("orig_ip_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes"), max("orig_bytes" / nullif("orig_pkts", 0)) FILTER (WHERE "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes"), arg_max(uid, "orig_bytes" - "orig_ip_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes"), sum(CASE WHEN "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), max("resp_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes"), max("resp_ip_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes"), max("resp_bytes" / nullif("resp_pkts", 0)) FILTER (WHERE "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes"), arg_max(uid, "resp_bytes" - "resp_ip_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes")
    FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2018/**/*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
    GROUP BY label_class ORDER BY 2 DESC

findings.title: 3 capture(s) begin at an identical timestamp
findings.detail: Captures sharing a first timestamp to the millisecond did not begin at the same moment by chance -- they contain the same traffic. The flows are counted more than once in every class total, and because the labelling predicate has no capture term, one schedule window labels all the copies. This is the strongest evidence that the capture folders are not the independent recordings their names claim.
findings.repro:
SELECT capture, count(*) AS n, min(ts) AS ts_min, max(ts) AS ts_max
    FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2018/**/*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
    WHERE ts IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY capture ORDER BY 3

findings.title: 5 capture pair(s) overlap in wall-clock time, the worst by 59.36 hours
findings.detail: Labelling matches on time and endpoints only, so a window selects a wall-clock interval across every capture at once. Where two captures cover the same second, a rule written for one of them silently claims traffic from the other, and no capture-level correction can separate them afterwards. It also rules out `capture` as a split key: the overlapping traffic would appear in both train and test.
findings.repro:
SELECT capture, count(*) AS n, min(ts) AS ts_min, max(ts) AS ts_max
    FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2018/**/*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
    WHERE ts IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY capture ORDER BY 3

findings.title: dos/DoS-SlowHTTPTest misses 2 of 5 behavioural expectation(s), worst by 90.0%
findings.detail: The flows carrying this label do not behave the way the label names. Either the window is over the wrong traffic, or the band in expectations.yaml is wrong -- the measured rate and the floor it missed are both reported so the reader can tell which.

evidence.why: The whole point of the attack is to exhaust a web server's connection pool. A slow-DoS window whose traffic is on another port is a window over the wrong traffic -- this is the band that fails on 2018, where 105,550 flows in the dos class sit on port 21.
Partial headers, dripped. Never a full request.
The socket is held, not fed. PROVISIONAL -- the profile pools the slow and fast DoS variants, so this is reasoned rather than measured.
PROVISIONAL, and the floor is deliberately low. Slow-DoS connections that are still open when the capture ends are logged by Zeek with a truncated duration, so this cannot be asserted strongly.
Single-source by definition, so the flow count per source host is what separates dos from ddos.

findings.repro:

       sum(CASE WHEN ("id.resp_p" IN (80, 443, 8080)) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS web_port,
       sum(CASE WHEN (coalesce(duration, 0) >= 5.0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS held_open
FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2018/**/*.parquet', union_by_name=true)
WHERE label_class = 'dos' AND label_raw = 'DoS-SlowHTTPTest'

findings.title: duration is null for 6.91% of benign flows
findings.detail: 4,055,142 flow(s) carry no duration. The EDA spec coalesces this feature's nulls to 0, so those flows are indistinguishable from flows that genuinely measured zero, and a class whose zero mass is really missing data will look flood-shaped whether or not it is. Nothing here says the labels are wrong -- it constrains which features a downstream claim about the affected classes may rest on, and requires that nulls be excluded explicitly rather than read as zeros.
findings.repro: SELECT label_class, count(*), sum(CASE WHEN "duration" IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2018/**/*.parquet') GROUP BY 1

findings.title: 4 quarantine region(s) overlap 4 scheduled attack window(s) in both time and endpoints
findings.detail: The schedule claims infiltration against these hosts in these minutes while the manifest declines to adjudicate the same flows. Both cannot stand: a window is either evidence of what happened there or it is not. Read each region's justification below and either narrow the region to the span the schedule does not cover, or withdraw the window.

evidence.justification: CIC describes Infiltration as two stages — "First level: Dropbox download in a windows machine. Second Level: Nmap and portscan" — and Table 2 publishes only the first. It names the infected host in the Victim column (172.31.69.24 on 28-02, 172.31.69.13 on 01-03), but never the scan targets and never a separate window for the second stage. The internal scan is therefore unlabellable from the schedule: we cannot say which flows it produced, so every one of them falls to benign by the closed-world assumption. That default is not neutral here. The attack rules match 8 flows across roughly 4.5 scheduled hours, while these windows carry on the order of 175,000 unmatched flows per 10-minute bucket — a benign class certified by nothing but the absence of a published target list. The 8 matched flows are no better founded than the unmatched ones: none of them completed a connection (conn_state OTH 50% / S1 37.5% / RSTR 12.5%) and the longest runs 13,254.7 s against a 5,820 s window, a 2.28x overrun, so they are mid-stream traffic caught by a time window rather than an observed attack (B11). They sit inside these regions and are quarantined with everything else; `infiltration` therefore carries no adjudicable evidence in this dataset and must not be evaluated as a class (B10). DistriNet derives the two phases as running to 18:39 and 19:38, far past CIC's published 14:40 and 15:37, so even as declared these regions UNDER-cover the phase (A3). They are drawn at the published times because those are what the source states; the DistriNet finding is why the region cannot be read as an upper bound on the contamination. Widening them, or replacing them with real second-stage attack rules, is DEFERRED until sch.window_sweep has measured where this traffic actually stops in our own lake: the DistriNet end times are a third party's derivation and are recorded as the hypothesis that sweep should test, never as a transcribed fact. Scoped to the hosts CIC does name, so the rest of each day — which the schedule describes normally — stays adjudicated. These regions coincide with the four scheduled Infiltration windows by construction, so qtn.overlap_with_attack reports them: we are declining to adjudicate a span the schedule claims. That contradiction is real and this is its answer — the schedule's claim here amounts to 8 unfinished flows and accounts for none of the rest.

That contradiction is real and this is its answer — the schedule's claim here amounts to 8 unfinished flows and accounts for none of the rest.

findings.title: CICFlowMeter artefact probes ran over 62,341,777 flows and found none of the signatures
findings.detail: Reported because the negative result is the finding. Rosay et al. (ICISSP 2022) identified four artefact classes that CICFlowMeter writes into every CSV it generates -- constant bulk features from an integer division, ARP frames read as IPv4 traffic between 8.0.6.4 and 8.6.0.1, non-TCP/UDP packets collapsed to protocol 0 with ports 0, and TCP flows cut at the first FIN whose halves can end up labelled differently -- and stated that every dataset shipping CICFlowMeter CSVs carries them, CIC-IDS-2017, CSE-CIC-IDS-2018 and CIC-DDoS-2019 included. Talos does not use those CSVs; the lake is Zeek output over the original pcaps. This check is the measurement behind that claim, so that 'our features do not carry the published artefacts' is a reading rather than an assertion. Probe 1 has no literal equivalent in Zeek's schema and is reported as inapplicable rather than faked.

evidence.artefact: bulk features constant through an integer-division fault
evidence.measured: no literal translation: Zeek has no bulk features. Numeric counters with zero variance are reported instead and never escalate
flows whose id.orig_h or id.resp_h is one of the ARP artefact addresses

evidence.artefact: non-TCP/UDP IPv4 collapsed to protocol 0 with ports 0
evidence.measured: flows with an absent or zero protocol and both ports zero, excluding the 8.0.6.4 family

evidence.artefact: TCP flow cut at the first FIN, halves labelled differently
evidence.measured: connections with a FIN in both directions that appear more than once under conflicting label_binary values

findings.title: 93,677 authentication record(s) observed across 2 brute_force window(s)
findings.detail: Authentication activity Zeek parsed inside the windows the schedule calls credential guessing, set beside the number of flows those windows were labelled with. A window with far fewer records than flows is mostly connections that never reached authentication.
findings.repro:
WITH rules AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES
        (1, 'SSH-Bruteforce', 'brute_force', 1518631260.0, 1518636720.0, ['172.31.70.6', '13.58.98.64', '172.31.69.25', '18.217.21.148'], CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR))
      ) AS t(rid, rname, rclass, t0, t1, eps, vpfx)),
          ev AS (SELECT "ts", "uid", "id.orig_h", "id.resp_h", "auth_attempts", "auth_success", "client" FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/parquets/cic-ids-2018/**/ssh.parquet', union_by_name=true)
        WHERE ts IS NOT NULL AND ts >= 1518631260.0 AND ts < 1518636720.0)
          SELECT r.rid, count(*) AS records,
                 count(DISTINCT e."uid") AS uids,
                 sum(coalesce(e."auth_attempts", 0)) AS attempts,
                 max(e."auth_attempts") AS max_attempts, sum(CASE WHEN e."auth_success" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successes,
                 count(DISTINCT e."id.orig_h") AS sources
          FROM rules r JOIN ev e ON e.ts >= r.t0 AND e.ts < r.t1
          AND (coalesce(list_contains(r.eps, e."id.orig_h"), false)
            OR coalesce(list_contains(r.eps, e."id.resp_h"), false)
            OR coalesce(starts_with(e."id.orig_h", r.vpfx), false)
            OR coalesce(starts_with(e."id.resp_h", r.vpfx), false)
            OR (r.eps IS NULL AND r.vpfx IS NULL))
          GROUP BY r.rid ORDER BY r.rid
